citation.title: Topology Optimization via Frequency Tuning of Neural Design Representations
citation.authors: Nikan Doosti; Julian Panetta; Vahid Babaei
citation.version_coded: author-hosted version of the conference paper

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Fourier-feature neural design representations produce mesh-independent structures and stiffness comparable to or better than voxel-based classical FEM optimization, with additional frequency-controlled designs.
claim.key_phrase: outperform or be on par with standard FEM-based solutions
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No speed-up claim is made; the authors state that their method takes longer to compute.
claim.alternatives: Sections 5.4 and 6 report quality comparisons and that the proposed optimizer needs 5,000 iterations versus about 300 for voxel/CNN baselines.

baseline.implementation: Authors' voxel baseline based on standard FEM/SIMP; comparison also includes CNN parameterization
baseline.solver: Sparse Cholesky for 2D; multigrid-preconditioned conjugate gradient for 3D
baseline.hardware_classical: AMD Ryzen 5950X CPU; 3D neural calculations used an NVIDIA Quadro RTX 8000 GPU
baseline.hardware_ml: AMD Ryzen 5950X CPU and NVIDIA Quadro RTX 8000 GPU
baseline.problem_size: 2D MBB 300 × 100 and bridge 250 × 125; 3D bridge 320 × 160 × 80 and cantilever 256 × 128 × 128
baseline.classical_iterations: Voxel-based and CNN baselines converge in about 300 iterations; Section 5.4
baseline.classical_time: FE solve averages 0.161 s/iteration (300 × 100 MBB) and 0.164 s/iteration (250 × 125 bridge); Section 6
baseline.ml_time: No total ML runtime. In 3D, network evaluation/backpropagation approaches but does not exceed the elasticity solve time per iteration; Section 6
baseline.training_time: Per-problem optimization, generally 5,000 iterations; not offline training
baseline.data_generation_cost: not applicable; no offline training dataset
baseline.quality_gap: Proposed method quantitatively matches or exceeds voxel/CNN results in stiffness; no single summary gap stated (Section 5.4)

R1.evidence: The primary outcome is design quality; Section 7 states that the method takes longer to converge than SIMP, so no speed advantage is asserted.

R2.evidence: No speed advantage is claimed; Section 6 reports sparse Cholesky in 2D and multigrid-preconditioned CG in 3D for FE solves.

R3.evidence: The network is optimized separately for each problem; there is no offline training cost (Sections 4–6).

R4.evidence: Sections 5–6 evaluate compliance through FE solves and enforce volume with reported violation below 10⁻⁴, but do not report failure/infeasibility rates.

reporting.n_test_cases: Multiple 2D and 3D benchmark/load examples; exact total not summarized

notes: This is a quality-stratum paper; it explicitly reports slower convergence than classical SIMP for simple problems.
